entry_json.definition: to stop doing something before it is finished, or to leave a person or place permanently
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The council abandoned the project once the costs doubled.
example_sentences: Many families abandoned the village after the flooding.
She abandoned her law degree in the second year and retrained as a nurse.

contexts.text: Governments should not abandon public transport schemes simply because they are expensive.
I abandoned the idea of driving to work after about a month of traffic.
The study was abandoned when the funding was withdrawn.

confusables.difference: Give up is the everyday spoken equivalent; abandon is stronger and more formal, and suggests leaving something for good.
You cancel an event that was scheduled. You abandon something already under way.

entry_json.avoid: Do not say "abandon to do something". Abandon takes a noun object: abandon the plan, not abandon to plan.

entry_json.definition: complete and total, with no limit or exception
entry_json.own_context_sentence: No government has absolute control over the price of food.
example_sentences: The report says there is an absolute shortage of nurses, not just a bad distribution of them.
For me, honesty in a friend is an absolute requirement.

contexts.text: Free access to clean water should be treated as an absolute right rather than a privilege.
Getting eight hours of sleep is an absolute must for me before an exam.
The figures show an absolute increase of 4 million, though the percentage change is small.

confusables.difference: Total is the neutral everyday word. Absolute adds the sense of no exceptions and no limits, and sounds more formal.
Complete describes something with no part missing; absolute describes something with no restriction on it.

entry_json.avoid: In academic writing, an absolute figure means a raw number, not a percentage. Do not mix the two when describing a chart.

entry_json.definition: completely, or used to agree strongly with someone
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I am absolutely certain I posted the application before the deadline.
example_sentences: The tour guide was absolutely brilliant, honestly.
There was absolutely nothing left in the fridge by Sunday.

contexts.text: Yes, absolutely, I think children should learn a second language early.
The city centre was absolutely packed on the day of the festival.
The evidence is absolutely clear on this point.

confusables.difference: Completely works with almost any adjective. Absolutely goes with extreme adjectives: absolutely exhausted, not absolutely tired.
Very is used with ordinary adjectives (very tired), absolutely with extreme ones (absolutely exhausted). They do not swap.

entry_json.avoid: Avoid stacking it in an essay. Repeating absolutely in Task 2 reads as emotional rather than measured.

entry_json.definition: connected with education, especially study at a school or university
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Her academic results were strong enough for a scholarship.
example_sentences: The academic year here runs from September to June.
Some students are excellent academically but struggle to find work.

contexts.text: Schools now judge pupils on academic results alone, which ignores their practical skills.
I was never very academic at school; I preferred sport.
Academic achievement was measured using end-of-year examination scores.

confusables.difference: Educational describes anything that teaches you, including a museum trip. Academic points at formal study and its standards.
Academic can also mean of no practical use, but only in the phrase purely academic. Use theoretical for ideas without practice.

entry_json.avoid: Do not use academic to mean intelligent. A person can be very clever and not at all academic.

entry_json.definition: good enough, or allowed by the rules or by most people
entry_json.own_context_sentence: A two-hour delay is not acceptable on a service people pay this much for.
example_sentences: Handing work in a day late is acceptable here, as long as you explain why.
What counts as acceptable behaviour in one culture may offend in another.

contexts.text: Smoking in restaurants was once socially acceptable but is now banned almost everywhere.
The hotel was basic but perfectly acceptable for two nights.
Error rates below five per cent were treated as acceptable.

confusables.difference: Suitable means right for a purpose. Acceptable only means good enough to be allowed, which is a lower bar.
Satisfactory means it meets the requirement; acceptable means people will tolerate it. Acceptable is the weaker praise.

entry_json.avoid: Acceptable is faint praise. If you mean something is good, say effective or suitable instead.

entry_json.definition: the chance or right to use something or reach a place
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Rural schools still have very limited access to fast internet.
example_sentences: Students get access to the library seven days a week.
Wheelchair access to the old building was added only last year.

contexts.text: Free access to higher education would widen participation among poorer families.
I only got access to a computer at home when I was about fourteen.
Access to clean drinking water rose from 62 to 89 per cent over the period.

confusables.difference: Entry is physically going in through a door. Access is the wider right or ability to use something, including services and information.

entry_json.avoid: It is access to something, never access of something. Also, access as a verb is formal and mostly used with data or systems.

entry_json.definition: a place for someone to live, stay or work in
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Student accommodation near the campus is far too expensive.
example_sentences: The university guarantees accommodation to all first-year students.
We found cheap accommodation about twenty minutes from the centre.

contexts.text: The shortage of affordable accommodation is pushing young workers out of major cities.
I share accommodation with two other students, which keeps the rent down.
I am writing to complain about the accommodation provided during the course.

confusables.difference: An apartment is one specific home. Accommodation is the general idea of somewhere to stay, and covers rooms, flats and hostels.
Housing is the policy word used about a whole population. Accommodation is what an individual person stays in.

entry_json.avoid: In British English accommodation is uncountable: say some accommodation, not an accommodation or accommodations.

entry_json.definition: to go somewhere with someone, or to happen at the same time as something
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Rising temperatures are usually accompanied by heavier rainfall.
example_sentences: Children under twelve must be accompanied by an adult.
The application should be accompanied by two references.

contexts.text: Rapid industrial growth is often accompanied by a sharp fall in air quality.
My sister accompanied me to the interview because I was nervous.
Each figure is accompanied by a short explanatory note.

confusables.difference: Go with is the natural spoken choice. Accompany is formal and is used mostly in rules, notices and academic writing.
Follow means one thing comes after another. Accompany means they happen together.

entry_json.avoid: Do not say accompany with a person. It is accompanied by, not accompanied with.

entry_json.definition: a written or spoken description of something that happened; also an arrangement with a bank or an online service
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Her account of the accident did not match the driver's.
example_sentences: I opened a bank account in the first week of term.
The book gives a detailed account of life in the city before the war.

contexts.text: Planners must take rising sea levels into account before approving coastal building.
I set up an account online and the whole thing took five minutes.
Eyewitness accounts of the event differ considerably.

confusables.difference: A report is usually official and organised. An account is simply one person's version of events and may be personal.
Story can suggest something invented. Account claims to be true.

entry_json.avoid: Take something into account, not take something in account. The phrase is fixed.

entry_json.definition: correct and exact, with no mistakes
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The forecast turned out to be surprisingly accurate.
example_sentences: We need accurate figures before we can decide anything.
His description of the building was accurate down to the colour of the door.

contexts.text: Policy decisions depend on accurate data about how people actually travel.
My watch is not very accurate, so I always set it five minutes fast.
The instrument is accurate to within two millimetres.

confusables.difference: Precise is about how fine the detail is; accurate is about whether it is right. A measurement can be precise and still wrong.
Correct is a simple yes or no. Accurate suggests closeness to the truth and allows degrees: fairly accurate, highly accurate.

entry_json.avoid: Do not use accurate about people's behaviour. A punctual person is not an accurate person.

entry_json.definition: to say that someone has done something wrong or illegal
entry_json.own_context_sentence: He was accused of copying another student's work.
example_sentences: Critics accuse the company of ignoring safety warnings.
I would never accuse anyone without proof.

contexts.text: Airlines are often accused of underestimating their true environmental cost.
She accused me of forgetting her birthday, which was fair enough.
Two officials were accused of falsifying the records.

confusables.difference: You blame someone for a result: blame him for the delay. You accuse someone of an act: accuse him of stealing.
Charge is the formal legal step taken by police. Accuse can be done by anyone, in or out of court.

entry_json.avoid: The pattern is accuse someone of doing something, with -ing. Not accuse someone to do something.

entry_json.definition: something good that you have succeeded in doing, especially after effort
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Finishing the course while working full time was a real achievement.
example_sentences: Winning a place at that university is a huge achievement for anyone.
The school celebrates achievement in sport as well as in exams.

contexts.text: Judging schools purely on academic achievement overlooks the pupils who develop slowly.
My proudest achievement is probably learning to swim at thirty.
Achievement was measured by final grade point average.

confusables.difference: Success is the general state of doing well. An achievement is one specific thing you completed.
Almost the same, but accomplishment is more common in American English; British IELTS writing usually prefers achievement.

entry_json.avoid: Do not say make an achievement. It is a great achievement, or you achieve something.

entry_json.definition: to accept or admit that something is true, or to say publicly that you have received something
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The report acknowledges that earlier estimates were too optimistic.
example_sentences: She acknowledged that the criticism was fair.
The company never acknowledged my email.

contexts.text: It must be acknowledged that private cars offer a freedom public transport cannot match.
He never acknowledges anyone in the corridor, which people find rude.
The authors acknowledge the limitations of their sample.

confusables.difference: Admit suggests you are confessing something that damages you. Acknowledge is neutral and simply accepts a fact.
Recognise means to see or identify something. Acknowledge means to say openly that it is true.

entry_json.avoid: In Task 2 this is the concession verb. Use it to grant the other side a point, then answer it with however.

entry_json.definition: to get or gain something, especially skills, knowledge or property
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Children acquire a second language far more easily than adults.
example_sentences: The firm acquired two smaller competitors last year.
You acquire a lot of practical knowledge in the first month of any job.

contexts.text: Students acquire far more from a term abroad than they do from a textbook.
I acquired a taste for strong coffee while I was studying in Italy.
Participants acquired the vocabulary over a six-week period.

confusables.difference: Obtain is used for documents and permission you apply for. Acquire is used for skills, habits and possessions built up over time.
Get is the everyday word. Acquire is the formal one and implies a gradual process, which is why it fits skills and knowledge.

entry_json.avoid: Acquire is too formal for small everyday things. You get a coffee, you do not acquire one.

entry_json.definition: real, as opposed to what is claimed, expected or imagined
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The actual cost was almost double the estimate.
example_sentences: Nobody knows the actual number of people living there.
The actual exam was easier than the practice papers.

contexts.text: The actual fall in unemployment was much smaller than the government claimed.
The actual journey only takes an hour; it is the waiting that kills you.
Actual values are shown in the table, with estimates in brackets.

confusables.difference: Actual does not mean current. Many learners transfer this from their own language. Current means happening now; actual means real.
Real is the everyday word and can describe genuine feelings. Actual is used to correct a wrong figure or assumption.

entry_json.avoid: This is a classic false friend. Actual never means at the moment. Use current or present for that.

entry_json.definition: an advertisement, especially a short one on television, online or in a newspaper
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I keep seeing the same ad every time I open the app.
example_sentences: There were so many ads before the video that I gave up.
She found the flat through an ad on a local website.

contexts.text: You cannot watch anything now without three ads first.
I got the job from an ad a friend sent me.
Advertisements aimed at children should be regulated more strictly.

confusables.difference: Same meaning, different register. Ad is spoken and informal; in Task 2 write advertisement or advertising.
A commercial is specifically an advertisement on television or radio. An ad can be anywhere.

entry_json.avoid: Keep ad out of Task 2. Write advertisement, advertising or marketing instead.

entry_json.definition: to change your behaviour to suit a new situation, or to change something so it works in a new one
entry_json.own_context_sentence: It took me a month to adapt to studying in a second language.
example_sentences: Older workers can adapt to new technology if they are trained properly.
The novel was adapted for television last year.

contexts.text: Countries that fail to adapt to changing energy markets will fall behind.
I adapted to the weather much faster than I expected.
The questionnaire was adapted from an earlier study.

confusables.difference: One letter apart and constantly confused. Adopt means to take something up: adopt a policy. Adapt means to change to fit.
Adjust is usually a small physical change: adjust the seat. Adapt is a deeper change over time.

entry_json.avoid: Adapt to something, not adapt with something. And do not write adopt when you mean adapt.

entry_json.definition: a thing that is added, or the act of adding something
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The new library is a welcome addition to the campus.
example_sentences: In addition to the fee, you pay for materials.
The addition of a bus lane cut journey times by ten minutes.

contexts.text: In addition, remote working reduces the number of cars on the road each morning.
In addition to my job, I take an evening class twice a week.
The addition of a control group strengthened the design.

confusables.difference: In addition stands alone and is followed by a comma. In addition to needs a noun or -ing after it.
Besides is more conversational and can sound dismissive. In addition is the safe linker for Task 2.

entry_json.avoid: Do not write in addition of. It is in addition to, and what follows is a noun or an -ing form.

entry_json.definition: extra, added to what already exists
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Additional funding would allow the clinic to open at weekends.
example_sentences: There is an additional charge for luggage over 20 kilos.
Additional staff were brought in during the busiest month.

contexts.text: Additional investment in cycling infrastructure would reduce congestion at little cost.
They charged us an additional fee for changing the date.
Additional data were collected in the second phase.

confusables.difference: Same meaning; extra is the spoken form. Additional is the one that belongs in an essay or formal letter.
Further suggests continuing something already started (further research). Additional simply means more of the same.

entry_json.avoid: Additional is an adjective only. Do not write additionally when you mean an extra thing.

entry_json.definition: the work of managing and organising an institution, or the people who do it
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Too much of a teacher's week now goes on administration.
example_sentences: The university administration handles all visa paperwork.
Cutting administration costs freed up money for equipment.

contexts.text: A large share of the health budget disappears into administration rather than treatment.
The teaching was great; the administration was a nightmare.
Administration of the survey took four weeks.

confusables.difference: Management is about deciding direction and leading people. Administration is the paperwork and routine organising that follows.
In American English administration can mean the government of the day. In British IELTS writing, use government for that.

entry_json.avoid: Do not use administration to mean the act of governing a country in British English essays; use government or authorities.

entry_json.definition: to respect someone for what they are or do, or to look at something and enjoy it
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I admire anyone who can raise children and study at the same time.
example_sentences: We stood on the bridge admiring the view.
She is widely admired for her honesty.

contexts.text: Young people tend to admire figures who achieve fame quickly rather than those who work quietly for years.
The person I admire most is my grandmother, actually.
His work is still admired by architects today.

confusables.difference: Respect can be given from duty, to a rank or a law. Admire is warmer and comes from genuine approval.
Appreciate is about valuing something, often with thanks. Admire is about looking up to it.

entry_json.avoid: Admire someone for something, not admire someone about something.

entry_json.definition: to agree, often unwillingly, that something bad or embarrassing is true
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I have to admit I had never heard of the author before.
example_sentences: He admitted that he had not read the instructions.
She refused to admit she was wrong.

contexts.text: Even supporters of the policy admit that it has done little for the poorest households.
I will admit I was terrified before my first presentation.
The authors admit that the sample was small.

confusables.difference: Confess is heavier and suggests guilt, often about something serious. Admit covers small awkward truths too.
Acknowledge is neutral; admit implies the fact is unwelcome to you.

entry_json.avoid: Admit doing something, or admit that you did it. Not admit to do something.

entry_json.definition: to start using a method, idea or attitude; also to take another person's child legally as your own
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Several cities have adopted a car-free policy in the centre.
example_sentences: The committee adopted the proposal without a vote.
They adopted two children from the same family.

contexts.text: If more governments adopted a four-day week, productivity might not fall as much as feared.
Our office adopted flexible hours last year and nobody wants to go back.
The method was adopted from earlier work in the field.

confusables.difference: Adopt is to take something on as it is. Adapt is to change it so it fits. Adopt a policy, adapt a method.
Accept means to agree to receive or believe something. Adopt means to put it into practice.

entry_json.avoid: The commonest error in the whole list: writing adopt when you mean adapt. Adopt = take up, adapt = change.

entry_json.definition: progress or a development, especially in knowledge or technology
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Advances in solar technology have made it far cheaper than coal.
example_sentences: Medical advances have added years to average life expectancy.
You have to book in advance to get the cheap fare.

contexts.text: Recent advances in artificial intelligence raise questions no law currently answers.
I always book train tickets in advance because they double on the day.
Advances in imaging allowed far more precise measurement.

confusables.difference: Progress is uncountable and describes the general movement forward. An advance is one countable step: three major advances.
An improvement makes an existing thing better. An advance usually brings something genuinely new.

entry_json.avoid: In advance is a fixed phrase and never takes the. Not in the advance.

entry_json.definition: at a high level, or using the most modern methods and ideas
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The course is aimed at advanced learners rather than beginners.
example_sentences: The hospital uses fairly advanced scanning equipment.
I reached an advanced level in Spanish before I stopped studying it.

contexts.text: Wealthier countries have access to advanced medical equipment that poorer ones cannot afford.
I am at an advanced level in reading but my speaking is well behind.
Advanced statistical methods were used to control for age.

confusables.difference: Developed describes countries and economies. Advanced describes technology, courses and skill levels.
Modern only means of the present time. Advanced means ahead of what most people have.

entry_json.avoid: Do not say advanced age to mean modern. Advanced age means old, which is a different meaning entirely.

entry_json.definition: to tell someone what you think they should do
entry_json.own_context_sentence: My tutor advised me to apply a year earlier.
example_sentences: Doctors advise cutting down on salt rather than cutting it out.
I would advise anyone visiting to avoid August.

contexts.text: Experts advise that children under two should not be given tablets at all.
A friend advised me to take the earlier train, and she was right.
Please advise me of the documents required.

confusables.difference: Advise is the verb with a /z/ sound; advice is the noun with an /s/ sound. Give advice, but advise someone.
Recommend suggests one good option among several. Advise carries more authority and often warns against something.

entry_json.avoid: Advise someone to do something. Not advise someone doing, and never advice as a verb.

entry_json.definition: an event or matter, especially a public one; in the plural, matters of a particular kind
entry_json.own_context_sentence: How a country educates its children is not purely a private affair.
example_sentences: The whole affair was reported for weeks in the newspapers.
She studied international affairs before joining the ministry.

contexts.text: Climate change is no longer a domestic affair; no country can solve it alone.
I try to keep up with current affairs by listening to the radio.
The report examines the state of financial affairs at the end of the year.

confusables.difference: An event is one thing that happens at a time and place. An affair is a whole situation, often with several parts and some controversy.
An issue is a topic people argue about. An affair is the episode itself, including what people did.

entry_json.avoid: In the singular, an affair can also mean a secret romantic relationship. Keep to fixed phrases like current affairs to avoid the misreading.

entry_json.definition: to have enough money or time for something
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Most graduates cannot afford to buy in the city where they work.
example_sentences: We could not afford a car when I was a child.
I cannot afford to miss another class.

contexts.text: Families on average incomes can no longer afford housing near their workplaces.
I could not really afford the trip, but I went anyway.
Households were asked whether they could afford to heat every room.

confusables.difference: Manage is about coping in general. Afford is specifically about having the money or the time to spare.
Allow is about permission. Afford is about resources.

entry_json.avoid: Afford almost always appears with can, could or be able to. Do not write I afford a new laptop.

entry_json.definition: at a later time, after the event you have just mentioned
entry_json.own_context_sentence: We visited the museum first and had lunch afterwards.
example_sentences: The lecture finishes at four and there is a discussion afterwards.
He apologised afterwards, but the damage was done.

contexts.text: The policy was introduced in 2010 and abandoned shortly afterwards.
We had dinner and went for a walk afterwards.
Participants were interviewed immediately afterwards.

confusables.difference: After needs an object: after the lecture. Afterwards stands alone at the end or start of a clause.
Later can point to any future time. Afterwards points specifically to after the thing just mentioned.

entry_json.avoid: Do not write afterwards the meeting. Use after the meeting, or put afterwards on its own.

entry_json.definition: of the age of; used before a number to say how old someone is
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The survey covered adults aged 18 to 34.
example_sentences: Classes are open to children aged seven and above.
A group of students aged around twenty were waiting outside.

contexts.text: Unemployment was highest among men aged 20 to 24 throughout the period.
There is a football club here for kids aged five upwards.
Applicants aged over 30 must provide proof of work experience.

confusables.difference: Old comes after the number: twenty years old. Aged comes before it: aged twenty.
Pronounced with two syllables, the aged means old people, which is a different word. In Task 1 always use the one-syllable aged plus a number.

entry_json.avoid: In Task 1 charts, write men aged 25 to 34, not men aged 25 to 34 years old. Do not double the age marker.

entry_json.definition: a business or organisation that provides a service, often arranging things for other people
entry_json.own_context_sentence: She found the job through a recruitment agency.
example_sentences: The environmental agency publishes air quality data every hour.
We booked the flat through a letting agency.

contexts.text: A single government agency should be responsible for monitoring water quality.
I used a travel agency once and honestly I would just book online now.
Data were supplied by the national statistics agency.

confusables.difference: An agent is one person. An agency is the organisation they work for.
Any business is a company. An agency specifically acts on behalf of somebody else.

entry_json.avoid: In IELTS writing, agency in the sense of personal control is C1 and rare. Stick to the organisation meaning.

entry_json.definition: a list of things to be discussed at a meeting, or a set of aims someone is trying to achieve
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Climate policy is now high on the political agenda in most countries.
example_sentences: The first item on the agenda was the budget.
Critics claim the newspaper has its own agenda.

contexts.text: Youth unemployment should be at the top of the government's agenda.
We had about ten things on the agenda and got through three.
The research agenda has shifted towards prevention rather than treatment.

confusables.difference: A schedule is about times: when things happen. An agenda is about topics: what will be discussed.
A plan says how something will be done. An agenda lists what matters.

entry_json.avoid: Saying someone has an agenda implies a hidden motive. Do not use it neutrally about a person's plans.

entry_json.definition: a person whose job is to arrange things for other people or companies
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Our estate agent showed us four flats in one morning.
example_sentences: A travel agent can sometimes find fares that websites miss.
The singer's agent handles all interview requests.

contexts.text: Online platforms have reduced the role of the travel agent almost to nothing.
We found our flat through an agent, which cost us a month's rent.
Insurance agents were interviewed as part of the study.

confusables.difference: An agency is the organisation; an agent is the individual working for it.
Representative is broader and includes anyone speaking for a group. An agent arranges transactions for a fee.

entry_json.avoid: In British English, the person who sells houses is an estate agent, not a realtor.

entry_json.definition: behaving in an angry or threatening way; also very forceful in pursuing something
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Aggressive driving is behind a large share of urban accidents.
example_sentences: He becomes aggressive when he is tired.
The company took an aggressive approach to expansion.

contexts.text: There is little evidence that violent games make children permanently aggressive.
Some drivers here are really aggressive at roundabouts.
Aggressive behaviour was recorded using a standard observation scale.

confusables.difference: Assertive is positive: saying clearly what you want. Aggressive is negative: threatening or attacking. Do not praise someone as aggressive.
Angry is a feeling. Aggressive is how someone acts on it towards others.

entry_json.avoid: Aggressive is almost always a criticism when describing people. Use assertive or determined for the positive sense.

entry_json.definition: an arrangement that two or more people or groups accept, or the state of sharing an opinion
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The two sides finally reached an agreement on working hours.
example_sentences: There is general agreement that the system needs reform.
We signed a twelve-month rental agreement.

contexts.text: International agreements on emissions mean nothing without enforcement.
My flatmate and I have an agreement about the kitchen.
There is broad agreement in the literature on this point.

confusables.difference: A contract is a legal document you can be sued over. An agreement can be informal and spoken.
Deal is the informal spoken word, often about money. Agreement is the neutral one for writing.

entry_json.avoid: Reach or come to an agreement, not do an agreement.

entry_json.definition: in front, or in the future; also further forward in progress
entry_json.own_context_sentence: There is a long summer ahead before term starts again.
example_sentences: Plan ahead if you want a cheap fare.
She is a year ahead of me on the same course.

contexts.text: Looking ahead, cities will need to plan for far hotter summers.
I never plan ahead; I just book things the week before.
China remained ahead of every other country in the chart throughout the period.

confusables.difference: Forward is about physical direction. Ahead often means in time or in a ranking.
In front of is a preposition needing an object. Ahead of is used for time and progress as well as position.

entry_json.avoid: Ahead of, not ahead from. And ahead of schedule means early, not in the schedule.

entry_json.definition: help, especially money, food or equipment given to countries or people in need
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Foreign aid works best when it is spent on local infrastructure.
example_sentences: Emergency aid reached the region within four days.
The charity provides aid to families who have lost their homes.

contexts.text: Rather than sending food aid indefinitely, wealthy nations should invest in local agriculture.
There was an appeal on the radio for aid after the earthquake.
Aid spending is shown as a percentage of gross national income.

confusables.difference: Help is the everyday word for anything from lifting a bag upwards. Aid is formal and usually organised, official and large-scale.
Support can be emotional or political. Aid is material: money, food, medicine.

entry_json.avoid: Aid is uncountable in this sense. Do not write aids, which means something different entirely.

entry_json.definition: the purpose of something, or what you are trying to achieve
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The main aim of the scheme is to get more people cycling.
example_sentences: My aim this year is to read one book a month.
The two policies have the same aim but very different methods.

contexts.text: The aim of compulsory education is not only to pass on knowledge but to prepare citizens.
My aim is to work abroad for a couple of years.
The aim of the study was to test whether sleep affects recall.

confusables.difference: A goal is usually specific and measurable, with a finish line. An aim is the broader purpose behind it.
Objective is the most formal of the three and usually appears in lists in reports.

entry_json.avoid: With the aim of is followed by an -ing form: with the aim of reducing traffic, not with the aim to reduce.

entry_json.definition: any vehicle that flies, including planes and helicopters
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Modern aircraft burn far less fuel per passenger than those of thirty years ago.
example_sentences: Three aircraft were grounded because of the storm.
The airport can handle the largest aircraft in service.

contexts.text: Aircraft emissions are hard to reduce because there is no practical alternative fuel yet.
The aircraft was tiny, about twenty seats.
Aircraft movements at the airport doubled between 1995 and 2015.

confusables.difference: Plane is the ordinary spoken word. Aircraft is the technical or formal term and also covers helicopters.
A flight is the journey. An aircraft is the machine.

entry_json.avoid: Aircraft has no plural -s. Write three aircraft, never three aircrafts.

entry_json.definition: a device that makes a noise to warn people or wake them; also a feeling of fear about a danger
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The fire alarm went off twice during the exam.
example_sentences: I set three alarms and still slept through them.
There is no cause for alarm; the water is safe to drink.

contexts.text: The rapid loss of insect species has raised alarm among biologists.
My alarm goes off at six but I never get up before half past.
Smoke alarms reduced fire deaths by nearly half over the period.

confusables.difference: A warning is information telling you about a danger. An alarm is the device or the reaction to it.

entry_json.avoid: Set an alarm and an alarm goes off. It does not open or ring off.

entry_json.definition: a collection of songs released together, or a book for keeping photographs in

The band released the album online only.

contexts.text: I usually listen to a whole album rather than single tracks.
We looked through my grandmother's photo album for hours.
Streaming has changed how albums are written and released.

confusables.difference: Record is the older word and can mean the physical disc. Album is the collection of songs itself.

entry_json.avoid: Album is a concrete everyday noun. It fits Speaking Part 1 and 2 far better than Task 2.

entry_json.definition: drinks such as beer and wine that can make you drunk
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Raising the price of alcohol does reduce how much people drink.

The event is open to under-18s, so no alcohol is served.

contexts.text: Governments could reduce health costs considerably by taxing alcohol more heavily.
I hardly drink alcohol at all during the week.
Alcohol consumption per head fell steadily after 2005.

confusables.difference: Drink as a noun can mean any beverage, or an alcoholic one from context. Alcohol is unambiguous and neutral, which suits writing.

entry_json.avoid: Alcohol is uncountable. Write a lot of alcohol, not many alcohols.

entry_json.definition: containing alcohol; as a noun, a person who cannot stop drinking
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The bar serves several non-alcoholic cocktails.
example_sentences: Alcoholic drinks are taxed at a much higher rate.
He admitted he was an alcoholic and asked for help.

contexts.text: Advertising for alcoholic drinks should be restricted in the same way as tobacco.
They only had non-alcoholic drinks, which suited me fine.
Sales of alcoholic beverages declined across all three countries.

confusables.difference: Alcohol is the noun for the substance. Alcoholic is the adjective, or a noun for a person with a drinking problem.

entry_json.avoid: Calling a person an alcoholic is a serious claim. In neutral writing prefer people with alcohol dependency.

entry_json.definition: to change something, usually slightly, or to become different
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Nothing the government did significantly altered the trend.
example_sentences: The plans were altered after residents complained.
Working nights completely altered my sleep pattern.

contexts.text: Remote working has altered the way city centres are used during the week.
I had to get the jacket altered because the sleeves were too long.
Removing the outliers did not alter the result.

confusables.difference: Change is the everyday word and covers everything. Alter is formal and usually means a partial adjustment, not a replacement.

entry_json.avoid: Alter is transitive or intransitive but never takes to. Write it altered the plan, not it altered to the plan.

entry_json.definition: very surprised, usually in a positive way

She was amazed by the size of the library.

contexts.text: I was amazed at how friendly people were when I first arrived.

Visitors are often amazed by the scale of the site.

confusables.difference: Amazed describes how you feel; amazing describes the thing causing it. I was amazed, the view was amazing.

entry_json.avoid: Amazed is a strong adjective, so use absolutely with it, not very.

entry_json.definition: something you very much want to achieve, or the desire to succeed
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Her ambition was always to work in medical research.
example_sentences: My main ambition at the moment is to finish the degree.
He has plenty of ambition but very little patience.

contexts.text: Schools should encourage ambition without teaching children that only money counts as success.

Career ambitions were measured on a five-point scale.

confusables.difference: A dream may be unrealistic and passive. An ambition is something you are actively working towards.

entry_json.avoid: Achieve or fulfil an ambition. Not realise an ambition in the sense of noticing it.

entry_json.definition: determined to succeed; also describing a plan that aims for a great deal and may be hard to achieve
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The target is ambitious but not impossible.
example_sentences: She is ambitious and will not stay in that job long.
It was an ambitious plan for a city of that size.

contexts.text: The emissions target is ambitious, and without new funding it will not be met.
I would not say I am especially ambitious; I just like the work.
The programme set ambitious targets for enrolment.

confusables.difference: Determined is about persistence with one task. Ambitious is about wanting to rise or achieve a lot overall.

entry_json.avoid: About a plan, ambitious hints that it may fail. That is often exactly the nuance you want in Task 2.

entry_json.definition: to examine something in detail in order to understand or explain it
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The team analysed responses from over two thousand students.
example_sentences: Before you rewrite the essay, analyse why you lost the marks.
Software now analyses the data in seconds.

contexts.text: Before banning cars from city centres, planners should analyse who actually depends on them.
I analysed my spending for a month and it was quite depressing.
The interviews were analysed for recurring themes.

confusables.difference: Examine is looking closely at something. Analyse means breaking it into parts to explain how it works.
Task 1 asks you to describe data. Analysing it, in the sense of explaining causes, loses marks there.

entry_json.avoid: British spelling is analyse; analyze is American. Keep one spelling system across the whole exam.

entry_json.definition: a detailed examination of something in order to understand it
entry_json.own_context_sentence: A closer analysis of the figures tells a different story.
example_sentences: The analysis showed no link between the two.
Her analysis of the poem was the best in the class.

contexts.text: A careful analysis of household energy use reveals where the largest savings lie.
They did a whole analysis of our team's workload, which changed nothing.
Statistical analysis was performed using standard software.

confusables.difference: Analysis is the noun with /s/; analyse is the verb with /z/. Carry out an analysis, or analyse the data.
A summary shortens what is there. An analysis explains what it means.

entry_json.avoid: The plural is analyses, pronounced /əˈnæləsiːz/. Do not write analysises.

entry_json.definition: the strong feeling you have when something is unfair or when someone has treated you badly
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The decision provoked real anger among local residents.
example_sentences: He struggled to control his anger in meetings.
There was public anger at the size of the fare increase.

contexts.text: The plan was withdrawn after widespread public anger about the cost.
I find it easier to deal with anger now than when I was younger.
Anger was the emotion most frequently reported by participants.

confusables.difference: Anger is the noun and takes no article when general: public anger. Angry is the adjective: people were angry.
Annoyance is mild and short. Anger is strong and can last.

entry_json.avoid: Anger is uncountable. Write a great deal of anger, not many angers.

entry_json.definition: the space between two lines that meet, measured in degrees; also a particular way of looking at a problem
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Looked at from another angle, the policy has clearly worked.
example_sentences: The panels are set at an angle of about thirty degrees.
The article approaches the housing crisis from an unusual angle.

contexts.text: Viewed from an economic angle, immigration has been a net benefit to most host countries.
I had never thought about it from that angle before.
The camera was mounted at a fixed angle above the road.

confusables.difference: Perspective is the more common academic word for a point of view. Angle is slightly informal in that sense and suits speaking.
A corner is the place where two edges meet. An angle is the measurement of the turn between them.

entry_json.avoid: In Task 2, from a different perspective reads better than from a different angle.

entry_json.definition: the date on which an important event happened in a previous year
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The city marked the hundredth anniversary of the flood with an exhibition.
example_sentences: Our tenth wedding anniversary is next month.
The company celebrated its fiftieth anniversary quietly.

contexts.text: Public anniversaries help a country remember events that later generations never lived through.
We usually go out somewhere nice for our anniversary.
The museum opened on the anniversary of the treaty.

confusables.difference: A birthday is for a person's own birth. An anniversary is the yearly return of any other event.
The celebration is the event you hold; the anniversary is the date itself.

entry_json.avoid: Do not use anniversary for a person's birthday. That is a false friend in several European languages.

entry_json.definition: to tell people about something officially or publicly
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The university announced the new fees in March.
example_sentences: They announced the results at nine o'clock.
She announced that she was leaving at the end of term.

contexts.text: The government announced the scheme without explaining how it would be funded.
They announced the delay just as we got to the platform.
The findings were announced at a conference in 2019.

confusables.difference: Say is any speaking. Announce is public and official, and the audience did not know beforehand.
Declare is stronger and more formal, used for war, independence and results. Announce is the ordinary official word.

entry_json.avoid: Do not write announce someone something. It is announce something to someone.

entry_json.definition: a public or official statement giving people information
entry_json.own_context_sentence: There was an announcement about the platform change.
example_sentences: The company made an announcement about job cuts.
I could not hear the announcement over the noise.

contexts.text: The announcement of the ban came with no consultation period at all.
They kept making announcements but nobody could understand them.
An official announcement followed the publication of the report.

confusables.difference: An advertisement tries to sell you something. An announcement simply informs you.
A notice is usually written and displayed. An announcement is often spoken and one-off.

entry_json.avoid: Make an announcement, not do or say an announcement.

entry_json.definition: to make someone slightly angry
entry_json.own_context_sentence: What annoys me most is people talking on the phone in the quiet carriage.
example_sentences: It annoys her when I leave the light on.
I did not mean to annoy anyone.

contexts.text: It annoys me when people cycle on the pavement.
The noise from upstairs annoyed us for months before we said anything.
Persistent advertising can annoy customers rather than attract them.

confusables.difference: Annoy is mild irritation. Anger is strong and serious. Do not swap them, the difference is one of degree.
Bother means to disturb or trouble someone; annoy means to irritate them.

entry_json.avoid: Annoy is fairly informal. In Task 2, prefer irritate, frustrate or cause frustration.

entry_json.definition: slightly angry about something
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I was annoyed with myself for missing the deadline.
example_sentences: He got annoyed when nobody replied to his message.
She was annoyed at the way the complaint was handled.

contexts.text: I get annoyed with myself if I waste a whole morning.
My neighbours were annoyed about the building work, understandably.
Passengers were annoyed by the lack of information.

confusables.difference: Annoyed is how you feel. Annoying is what causes the feeling. I was annoyed, the delay was annoying.
Annoyed is mild and passes. Angry is strong.

entry_json.avoid: You are annoyed WITH a person, ABOUT a situation and AT or BY an action. Do not use annoyed of.

entry_json.definition: making you feel slightly angry
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The most annoying thing about the app is that it logs you out constantly.
example_sentences: It is annoying when the bus arrives early.
That is a really annoying habit.

contexts.text: The annoying part is that you have to queue twice.
It is annoying when shops close before people finish work.
Frequent pop-ups are one of the most irritating features of free apps.

confusables.difference: Annoying describes the cause; annoyed describes the person feeling it.
Irritating is slightly more formal and safer in writing; annoying belongs in speech.

entry_json.avoid: Annoying is spoken register. In Task 2 write irritating, frustrating or inconvenient.

entry_json.definition: happening once every year, or measured over a year
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The annual rainfall in the region has fallen by a fifth.
example_sentences: Staff get twenty-five days of annual leave.
The annual report is published every March.

contexts.text: Average annual income rose steadily between 2000 and 2015.
We have an annual family get-together in the summer.
Annual spending on public transport should be tied to population growth.

confusables.difference: Almost identical, but annual is the formal one used in reports and charts. Yearly sounds conversational.
Every year is a phrase; annual is an adjective before a noun. Do not write the every year report.

entry_json.avoid: The adverb is annually, not annualy. Spending rose annually, or annual spending rose.

entry_json.definition: worried and nervous about something that might happen
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Many students feel anxious in the week before results.
example_sentences: I was anxious about speaking in front of the class.
Parents are anxious that the changes will disadvantage their children.

contexts.text: Constant comparison on social media leaves many teenagers anxious about their appearance.
I always get a bit anxious before a long flight.
Anxious participants performed worse on the timed task.

confusables.difference: Nervous is short-term and often physical, before a specific event. Anxious is longer-lasting worry about an outcome.
Worried focuses on a particular problem. Anxious describes a general state, and is the word used in health contexts.

entry_json.avoid: Anxious to do something means eager, not worried. Keep anxious about for the worried meaning.

entry_json.definition: separated by distance or time, or into pieces
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The two towns are only ten kilometres apart.
example_sentences: My brother and I were born three years apart.
The chair fell apart after one winter outside.

contexts.text: Apart from the cost, there is nothing wrong with the proposal.
My best friend and I live about two hours apart now.
The two peaks in the graph are roughly a decade apart.

confusables.difference: Apart from means except for, and needs a noun after it. Apart alone means separated.
Separate is an adjective describing two distinct things. Apart describes the distance or gap between them.

entry_json.avoid: Apart is one word. A part means a piece of something, which is a different meaning altogether.

entry_json.definition: to say you are sorry for something you have done
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I apologised for missing the meeting.
example_sentences: He apologised to the whole class.
The airline apologised for the delay but offered nothing else.

contexts.text: I am writing to complain about the service and to ask that the company apologize formally.
I apologised straight away, which seemed to help.
Public figures are now expected to apologize quickly when they make a mistake.

confusables.difference: Apologize is the verb; apology is the noun. Make an apology, or apologize.
An excuse explains why you did it. An apology accepts that it was wrong.

entry_json.avoid: Apologize TO a person FOR a thing. Both prepositions are needed and they are not interchangeable. British writing may also spell it apologise.

entry_json.definition: easy to see or understand; or seeming to be true although possibly not
entry_json.own_context_sentence: It soon became apparent that the data had been collected badly.

The benefits of the scheme are apparent to everyone who uses it.

contexts.text: It quickly became apparent that the policy was helping wealthier households most.
It was apparent from her face that the news was bad.
The effect was apparent only in the older age group.

confusables.difference: Obvious is the everyday word and stronger. Apparent is formal and can carry a hint of doubt: his apparent enthusiasm.
Clear is neutral and safe. Apparent suits the phrase it became apparent that, which is excellent in Task 2.

entry_json.avoid: Watch the ambiguity. Her apparent success may mean she seems successful but is not. Use clear if you mean it certainly is so.

entry_json.definition: according to what you have heard or read, though you are not certain it is true
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Apparently the new library opens in September.
example_sentences: Apparently they are closing the road for six weeks.
He was apparently unaware that the deadline had changed.

contexts.text: Apparently the course is quite hard to get onto now.
Apparently they had already made the decision before the meeting.
The two studies apparently contradict each other, though the samples differ.

confusables.difference: Obviously means everyone can see it. Apparently means somebody told you and you have not checked. They are near opposites in certainty.

entry_json.avoid: Do not use apparently to introduce your own argument in Task 2. It signals you are not sure, which weakens the claim.

entry_json.definition: a serious public request for help or money; also the quality that makes something attractive
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The charity launched an appeal after the earthquake.
example_sentences: The appeal raised over two million pounds in a week.
I can see the appeal of living in a small town.

contexts.text: Streaming services have lost some of their appeal now that each film sits behind a separate subscription.
I can see the appeal of working from home, but I would miss people.
The campaign's appeal was strongest among viewers under 30.

confusables.difference: An attraction is usually a place you visit. Appeal is the abstract quality that draws people to something.
A request is ordinary and private. An appeal is public and urgent.

entry_json.avoid: In law, an appeal is a request to change a court decision. Make the sense clear from the surrounding words.

entry_json.definition: a formal written request for a job, place or permission; also a practical use of something
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I submitted my application two days before the deadline.
example_sentences: The university received four thousand applications for sixty places.
There are many practical applications for this technology.

contexts.text: The practical applications of this research extend well beyond medicine.
My application took about three hours to fill in.
Applications for the scheme rose sharply in the final year.

confusables.difference: Application is the noun, apply the verb. Make an application, or apply for a job.

entry_json.avoid: Apply FOR a job but apply TO a university. Make an application, do not do one.

entry_json.definition: an arrangement to meet or visit someone at a particular time
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I have a dentist's appointment on Thursday morning.

I made an appointment online, which was much easier than phoning.
Missed appointments cost the health service millions each year.

confusables.difference: A meeting is usually several people discussing work. An appointment is a booked slot with one professional.
You make a reservation at a restaurant or hotel. You make an appointment with a doctor or a hairdresser.

entry_json.avoid: Make an appointment, not take an appointment. That is a direct translation error from several languages.

entry_json.definition: to recognise the value of something, or to be grateful for it
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I really appreciate how much time you spent on this.
example_sentences: You only appreciate clean air after living in a polluted city.
I would appreciate a reply before Friday.

contexts.text: I would appreciate a full refund of the deposit.
I appreciate having a garden much more now than I did as a child.
Few people appreciate how much water is used to produce a single kilo of beef.

confusables.difference: Enjoy is about pleasure at the time. Appreciate is about recognising worth, often afterwards.
You thank a person directly. You appreciate a thing they did.

entry_json.avoid: I would appreciate it if you could... needs the it. Leaving it out is a common formal-letter error.

entry_json.definition: a way of dealing with a problem or task
entry_json.own_context_sentence: A gentler approach to discipline works better with younger children.
example_sentences: The two schools take completely different approaches to homework.
We need a fresh approach to the housing shortage.

contexts.text: A preventive approach to healthcare is far cheaper than treating illness once it appears.
My approach to revision is just to keep testing myself.
A mixed-methods approach was adopted for this study.

confusables.difference: A method is a specific set of steps. An approach is the broader attitude or strategy behind them.

entry_json.avoid: It is an approach TO a problem, not an approach OF a problem.

entry_json.definition: suitable or right for a particular situation, person or purpose
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Jeans would not be appropriate for a job interview here.
example_sentences: Choose language appropriate to your reader.
It seemed the appropriate moment to raise the question.

contexts.text: Schools must decide what content is appropriate for children of different ages.
I was not sure what was appropriate to wear, so I asked.
Appropriate statistical tests were selected for each variable.

confusables.difference: Almost interchangeable, but appropriate carries a sense of social correctness as well as practical fit.
Correct means factually right. Appropriate means socially or contextually right, which is a different judgement.

entry_json.avoid: Appropriate FOR a purpose, appropriate TO a situation. The stress differs from the verb: the adjective ends /-ət/, the verb /-eɪt/.

entry_json.definition: official permission, or the feeling that something is good
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The plan still needs approval from the city council.
example_sentences: The drug was given approval last year.
She was looking for her father's approval more than anything.

contexts.text: New building projects should not receive approval without an environmental assessment.
We had to get approval from the landlord before painting anything.
Ethical approval was obtained before data collection began.

confusables.difference: Permission is simply being allowed. Approval is formal and often means a body has examined and accepted something.

entry_json.avoid: Approval is usually uncountable here. Write obtain approval, not obtain an approval.

entry_json.definition: to officially agree to something, or to think that something is good
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The committee approved the budget without discussion.
example_sentences: My parents never really approved of my choice of subject.
The plans were approved in April.

contexts.text: Councils should not approve developments on land at risk of flooding.
My family did not entirely approve of me moving abroad.
The protocol was approved by an independent committee.

confusables.difference: Approve something means to give it official permission. Approve OF something means you think it is morally good. The preposition changes the meaning.

entry_json.avoid: This is the trap: the committee approved the plan, but my mother approved of the plan. Choose the preposition deliberately.

entry_json.definition: about; used before a number that is close but not exact
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Approximately one in five households has no car.
example_sentences: The journey takes approximately two hours.
Approximately 40 per cent of respondents were under 25.

contexts.text: Approximately 60 per cent of the city's electricity came from coal in 1990.
It takes approximately half an hour to walk into town.
Approximately two thirds of graduates now work in a field unrelated to their degree.

confusables.difference: Same meaning; about is spoken, approximately is written. In Task 1 approximately, around and roughly all work.
Exactly claims precision. Approximately admits the figure is rounded, which is safer when reading a chart.

entry_json.avoid: Do not write approximately about. One hedge is enough.

entry_json.definition: to happen or begin to exist, especially a problem or situation
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Problems arise when two departments use different systems.
example_sentences: Several questions arose during the discussion.
Should the need arise, we can extend the deadline.

contexts.text: Conflict arises when growing cities compete with farmland for the same water.
A few issues arose in the first week but we sorted them out.
The difficulty arises from the small size of the sample.

confusables.difference: Rise is used for numbers and levels going up: prices rise. Arise is used for problems and questions coming into existence.

entry_json.avoid: Arise has no object. Do not write the policy arose problems; write problems arose from the policy. Forms: arise, arose, arisen.

entry_json.definition: carrying a weapon, or involving weapons
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The country has not been involved in armed conflict for decades.
example_sentences: Armed police were stationed at the entrance.
The robbery was carried out by armed men.

contexts.text: Refugee numbers rise sharply wherever armed conflict lasts more than a year.
I had never seen armed police until I went through that airport.
Deaths from armed conflict fell over the twenty-year period.

confusables.difference: Military describes the organisation and its equipment. Armed describes anyone carrying weapons, including criminals.
Armed is factual: they have weapons. Dangerous is a judgement about risk.

entry_json.avoid: Armed forces is a fixed plural phrase. Do not write the armed force for a country's military.

entry_json.definition: weapons, especially those used by armies
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The country is one of the largest exporters of arms in the world.
example_sentences: An arms agreement was signed in 1991.
Spending on arms rose while spending on schools fell.

contexts.text: The arms trade profits from exactly the instability that aid programmes try to repair.
There was a documentary about the arms trade that really stayed with me.
Arms exports are shown by value in the second chart.

confusables.difference: The singular arm is the body part. Arms in the weapons sense exists only in the plural, in fixed phrases like arms trade.

entry_json.avoid: Only use arms for weapons inside a fixed phrase. Otherwise a reader will picture body parts.

entry_json.definition: to take someone to a police station because the police think they have committed a crime
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Two men were arrested at the scene.
example_sentences: He was arrested for driving without a licence.
Police arrested nobody, despite dozens of complaints.

contexts.text: Arresting people for minor drug offences fills prisons without reducing use.
Someone was arrested outside our building last week, apparently.
Arrest rates fell in every category except fraud.

confusables.difference: Catch is informal and just means to get hold of someone. Arrest is the legal act performed by police.
Arrest comes first and is temporary. Charging is the formal accusation that may follow.

entry_json.avoid: Arrested FOR a crime, not arrested BECAUSE OF a crime. The preposition is fixed.

entry_json.definition: the act of arriving somewhere, or the appearance of something new
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The arrival of cheap flights changed European tourism completely.
example_sentences: Our arrival was delayed by three hours.
On arrival, please report to reception.

contexts.text: The arrival of streaming services has all but ended the local video shop.
On arrival we discovered the hotel had cancelled our booking.
Arrivals at the airport increased by 12 per cent in 2018.

confusables.difference: Arrival is the noun; arrive is the verb. On arrival, or when we arrived.
Departure is leaving; arrival is getting there. Airports label the two boards this way.

entry_json.avoid: On arrival takes no article and no possessive. Not on the arrival or on my arrival at in formal notices.

entry_json.definition: made by people rather than occurring in nature, and often copying something natural
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Artificial lighting in offices affects how well people sleep.
example_sentences: The drink contains no artificial colours.
They built an artificial lake to store water for the summer.

contexts.text: Artificial intelligence will replace routine tasks long before it replaces judgement.
I try to avoid anything with artificial sweeteners.
An artificial reef was constructed to encourage fish stocks to recover.

confusables.difference: Fake means intended to deceive, and is negative. Artificial is neutral: an artificial lake is not pretending to be anything.
Synthetic refers to chemically manufactured materials. Artificial is broader and includes lakes, light and intelligence.

entry_json.avoid: Artificial can also describe insincere behaviour: an artificial smile. Keep the context clear so the reader is not misled.

entry_json.definition: connected with art, or having a natural skill in art
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The city has a strong artistic tradition going back centuries.
example_sentences: She is far more artistic than I am.
The building was praised for its artistic merit rather than its usefulness.

contexts.text: Cutting artistic subjects from the curriculum saves money now and costs creativity later.
I am not artistic at all, but I do enjoy going to galleries.
The artistic movement of the period is well documented.

confusables.difference: Creative covers all new thinking, including in science and business. Artistic points specifically at art, music and design.
Aesthetic is about beauty and appearance. Artistic is about the practice of art.

entry_json.avoid: Artistic describes people and traditions, not individual objects. A painting is not artistic; it has artistic merit.

entry_json.definition: feeling guilty or embarrassed about something you have done or about yourself
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I am ashamed to say I have never read a book in my second language.
example_sentences: He was ashamed of the way he had behaved.
Nobody should be ashamed of asking for help.

contexts.text: Students should not be made to feel ashamed of mistakes; that is how a language is learnt.
I am a bit ashamed of how much time I spend on my phone.
Respondents reported feeling ashamed rather than angry.

confusables.difference: Embarrassed is short and social: you go red. Ashamed is moral and deeper: you think you did something wrong.
Shy is a personality trait about meeting people. Ashamed is a reaction to something specific.

entry_json.avoid: Ashamed OF something, or ashamed TO DO something. Never ashamed for.

entry_json.definition: one part or feature of a situation, idea or problem
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The most difficult aspect of moving abroad is the paperwork.
example_sentences: We looked at every aspect of the proposal.

Damage to the ceiling was recorded in three of the rooms.

entry_json.avoid: Roof and ceiling are not interchangeable, though many languages use one word for both.

contexts.text: Public celebrations give a city a shared identity that no marketing campaign can buy.
The best celebration I have been to was my cousin's wedding.
The festival began as a celebration of the harvest.

confusables.difference: A party is informal and social. A celebration marks a specific occasion and can be public and formal.

entry_json.avoid: In celebration OF something. Countable: one celebration, several celebrations.

entry_json.definition: the smallest unit of a living thing; also a small room in a prison

Prisoners spend up to 22 hours a day in their cells.

contexts.text: Understanding how cells repair themselves may eventually make many current treatments unnecessary.
I remember looking at plant cells under a microscope at school.
Cell counts were recorded every twelve hours.

confusables.difference: Cell and sell sound identical but are unrelated. Only the spelling separates them.

entry_json.avoid: In British IELTS writing, say mobile phone. Cell phone will be understood but marks you as using American English.

entry_json.definition: in or near the middle of a place; also most important

Central London is now almost entirely car-free at weekends.

contexts.text: Education is central to any long-term strategy for reducing inequality.
Our flat is quite central, which is why the rent is what it is.
Central heating was installed in 78 per cent of homes by 1990.

confusables.difference: Central is the adjective, centre the noun. The city centre, but a central location.
Main means the largest or most used. Central in the figurative sense means most essential to the argument.

entry_json.avoid: Central TO something, not central OF something. And British spelling is centre, not center.

entry_json.definition: a formal public event held to mark an important occasion

example_sentences: The opening ceremony was watched by millions.
It was a short ceremony with only close family present.

contexts.text: Graduation ceremonies matter more to families than to the students, and that is the point of them.
My graduation ceremony was outdoors and it rained the whole time.
The ceremony is described in several contemporary sources.

confusables.difference: A celebration is joyful and may be informal. A ceremony follows a set order and is formal, whether happy or sad.
Event is any organised occasion. A ceremony specifically has a formal ritual structure.

entry_json.avoid: Hold or attend a ceremony. Do not write make a ceremony.

entry_json.definition: a line of connected metal rings; also a group of shops or hotels under one owner, or a connected series of events
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Independent bookshops struggle to compete with the big chains.
example_sentences: The bike was locked with a heavy chain.
A chain of events led to the delay.

contexts.text: The rise of coffee chains has made every high street in the country look identical.
There is a chain hotel near the station that is always cheapest.
Disruption to the supply chain affected every stage of production.

confusables.difference: A series is any set of things in order. A chain implies each link depends on the one before it.
A franchise is owned locally under a shared brand. A chain is usually owned centrally.

entry_json.avoid: Supply chain and chain of events are fixed phrases worth learning whole for Task 2.

entry_json.definition: the person in charge of a meeting, committee or company board
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The chairman opened the meeting twenty minutes late.
example_sentences: She was appointed chairman of the committee in 2019.
The chairman resigned after the report was published.
